newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's small companies want deal on debt, taxes.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's small companies want deal on debt, taxes.

text.p: Brazil's small business sector wants to renegotiate about $8.0 billion in debt, as well as favorable new tax rules, a deputy who represents small companies said.
"We want to set up talks over small company debt which would run parallel with negotiations over taxes," Dep. Augusto Nardes told reporters.
The government and representatives of small businesses are hammering out rules for a new, single tax bracket for companies earning up to 204,000 reais a year.

The two sides are trying to reach a middle ground between the companies' demands for tax-free status, included in legislation currently in Congress, and the government's insistence that such a move would cost $4.0 billion in revenues.
Nardes said he and other members of the so-called Parliamentary Front for Small Businesses were due to meet with presidential chief of staff Clovis Carvalho later on Wednesday to continue talks.

The battle also has political implications. The legislation that would have given Brazil's around four million small companies tax-free status was penned by Sen. Jose Sarney, a former president who presides over Congress.
Sarney has criticized the government over its economic policies and has said his legislation would create millions of new jobs.
